question: Should OpenClaw require UX flow-stage and recovery-path answers on every bug report, and add the optional UX impact prompt to feature requests, now that the paired ClawSweeper rubric has merged?
rationale: The YAML change is straightforward, but required public issue-form fields are a maintainer policy and contributor-friction choice rather than a code-correctness issue.

options.title: Merge the intake fields as proposed
options.body: Accept the two required bug-report dropdowns and optional textareas so future reports carry the UX blocker facts ClawSweeper now knows how to use.

options.title: Make the bug fields lighter
options.body: Ask for the bug-report UX fields to be optional or folded into the existing impact section if maintainers want less reporter friction.

options.title: Pause the intake change
options.body: Keep UX release-blocker classification manual for now if maintainers do not want issue forms to require this information.

recommendation.title: Merge the intake fields as proposed
recommendation.body: Accept the two required bug-report dropdowns and optional textareas so future reports carry the UX blocker facts ClawSweeper now knows how to use.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to both the current issue-template files and the final policy-threshold tightening in the paired merged ClawSweeper rubric PR.
